title: Dolmabahçe Palace & Beşiktaş: Planning the Visit
seoTitle: Dolmabahçe Palace Tickets 2026: Hours, Closures & Route
metaDescription: Plan your 2026 Dolmabahçe Palace visit: 2,000 TL ticket rules, Monday closures, Selamlık vs. Harem timing, and a Beşiktaş–Ortaköy route.
quickAnswer: Foreign visitor Dolmabahçe Palace tickets cost 2,000 TL in 2026 and include the Selamlık, Harem, and Painting Museum, while the Museum Pass Istanbul is not accepted for the main palace. Arrive at 09:00 Tuesday through Sunday (closed Mondays), budget 2.5 to 3 hours, and pair the palace with Beşiktaş and Ortaköy.

body.text: How does Dolmabahçe differ from Topkapı Palace?

Dolmabahçe Palace is a 19th-century monoblock European-style waterfront palace built under Sultan Abdülmecid, whereas Topkapı Palace is a 15th-century Ottoman courtyard complex overlooking the Golden Horn and Marmara Sea. Dolmabahçe displays crystal chandeliers, Hereke carpets, and gilded ceremonial halls; Topkapı showcases imperial kitchens, tiled pavilions, and four centuries of classical Ottoman statecraft.

Both residences operate under the [Presidency of National Palaces (Milli Saraylar)](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Lokasyon/3/Dolmabahce-Sarayi?culture=en), yet they reflect different eras. [Topkapı Palace](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Lokasyon/2/Topkapi-Sarayi) unfolds across four open-air courtyards where sultans governed from 1465 until the mid-1800s. Dolmabahçe concentrates 285 rooms, 44 halls, and 6 hamams inside one symmetrical 14,595-square-meter structure directly on the Bosphorus shore, blending Baroque, Rococo, and Neoclassical facades with a Turkish central-hall layout.

In 2026, foreign [Dolmabahçe Palace tickets](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Bilet/BiletAl) cost 2,000 TL (roughly €36–€40), while [Topkapı Palace combined entry](https://topkapipalacemuseum.com/topkapi-palace-tickets-hours-location-info) is 2,750 TL. Milli Saraylar also sells a 2,750 TL European-side combo (adding Yıldız Palace and kiosks) and a 3,500 TL Full Pass (excluding Topkapı).
How long does the Selamlık and Harem visit take?

Plan 2 to 2.5 hours for the Selamlık, Ceremonial Hall, Harem, and waterfront gardens, plus another 45 minutes if you enter the Painting Museum. Because all three sections come bundled on the single foreign-visitor ticket, arriving before 09:30 lets you clear the main reception halls before tour buses peak at 11:00.

The palace follows a strict one-way route starting in the Selamlık (Mabeyn-i Hümâyûn)—the administrative wing—climbing the Baccarat Crystal Staircase into the soaring Ceremonial Hall (Muayede Salonu). A short garden walk then leads to the quieter Harem, including the room where Mustafa Kemal Atatürk died on November 10, 1938.

items: 09:00–10:15: Clear security, collect the included audio guide (bring photo ID as deposit), and walk the Selamlık first.
10:15–11:00: Tour the Harem and pause along the marble Bosphorus quay.
11:00–11:45: Visit the Painting Museum in the former Crown Prince's Apartments for its collection of Ivan Aivazovsky seascapes.

body.text: Check the [official Milli Saraylar page](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Lokasyon/3/Dolmabahce-Sarayi?culture=en) before arrival, as the on-site Clock Museum undergoes periodic restoration closures.

Dolmabahçe Palace is closed every Monday, as well as January 1 and the first days of the two major Islamic holidays (Ramadan Bayram and the Feast of Sacrifice). Ticket offices operate Tuesday through Sunday from 09:00 to 17:00, and the palace grounds close at 17:30.

This Monday closure catches more Istanbul schedules off guard than almost any other error. Because Topkapı Palace closes on Tuesdays, schedule Topkapı on Monday and Dolmabahçe on Tuesday, or visit both between Wednesday and Sunday. Ride the T1 tram to Kabataş (a flat 5-minute walk north along the coast) or take the F1 funicular down from Taksim Square.
How do you pair it with Ortaköy and Beşiktaş?

Walk 15 minutes north along tree-lined Dolmabahçe Caddesi to Beşiktaş's market lanes for a proper lunch, then continue by short taxi, bus, or Bosphorus ferry to Ortaköy Square for late-afternoon light on the Büyük Mecidiye Mosque. Keep the route linear along the water to avoid Istanbul's notorious coastal cross-traffic.

Duck into the pedestrianized Beşiktaş Çarşı around the fish market for grilled seasonal fish or esnaf lokantası home cooking. From Beşiktaş pier, public ferries cross to Üsküdar and Kadıköy every 15 minutes if you want an Asian-side afternoon. Otherwise, head 2.5 kilometers north to Ortaköy to photograph the Neo-Baroque Ortaköy Mosque beneath the 15 July Martyrs Bridge, then depart before 17:30 when Çırağan Caddesi gridlocks.

faq.q: Can I buy Dolmabahçe Palace tickets online in advance?
faq.a: Yes. Purchase electronic tickets directly on the official [Milli Saraylar portal](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Bilet/BiletAl) or at the box office to avoid reseller markups above the 2,000 TL rate.

faq.q: Is the Museum Pass Istanbul valid at Dolmabahçe Palace?
faq.a: No. The Museum Pass covers Ministry of Culture sites, whereas Dolmabahçe is managed by the Presidency of National Palaces and requires its own Milli Saraylar ticket.

faq.q: Are photos allowed inside Dolmabahçe Palace?
faq.a: Non-flash handheld photography is permitted in most halls, but flash, tripods, and commercial video gear are prohibited.

faq.q: Is the Harem included in the standard foreign ticket?
faq.a: Yes. The 2,000 TL foreign-visitor ticket bundles the Selamlık, Harem, and Painting Museum into one combined entry.

faq.q: How early should I arrive to beat the ticket line?
faq.a: Arrive between 08:45 and 09:00 at opening; between 10:30 and 14:00, group coaches push security queues past 45 minutes.

faq.q: Can I visit Topkapı Palace and Dolmabahçe Palace on the same day?
faq.a: Technically yes Wednesday through Sunday, but six to seven hours of palace interiors causes heavy museum fatigue. Split them across two mornings.
